In this paper, we propose a novel data augmentation scheme to synthesize controllable and much less noisy data for cross-lingual NLI. This augmentation consists of two parts. One serves to encourage language adaptation by means of reordering source language words based on word alignments to better cope with typological divergency between languages, denoted as Reorder Augmentation (RA). Another seeks to enrich the set of semantic relationships between a premise and pertinent hypotheses, denoted as Semantic Augmentation (SA). Both are achieved by learning corresponding sequence-to-sequence (Seq2Seq) models.
